3. The present petition filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeks quashing of FIR No. 238/2020, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Ghazipur and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the court of Ms.
Shazadi Halima, learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahila Court (East), Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.
4. The marriage between petitioner no.1/husband and respondent no.2/wife was solemnized on 09.07.2011 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies.
5. No child was born out of the said wedlock.

Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2/complainant, the latter lodged an FIR against petitioners herein and Ms. Reeta Goel, (mother-in-law), who has since passed away.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the present proceedings, the parties have amicably settled their underlying disputes.
It is further submitted that petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2/complainant are now residing together peacefully in their matrimonial home.
8. Petitioners and complainant/respondent no. 2 are present before the Court and have been duly identified by their respective counsel, as well as the Investigating Officer ASI Rambir, P.S. Ghazipur.
9. The complainant/respondent No.2 states that the matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

She further states that she has been residing together peacefully with petitioner no. 1, in their matrimonial home, since, 28.05.2021.
10.
In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

11. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303, the Honble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable resolution of disputes by observing as under:-
"61.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ... In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceedings or continuation of criminal proceedings would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in the affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 09:32:43 12.

In view of the aforesaid circumstances, and the fact that the parties have put a quietus to the dispute, no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the present FIR No. 238/2020, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Ghazipur and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the court of Ms.
Shazadi Halima, , learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahila Court (East), Karkardooma Courts,
Delhi.

13. In the interest of justice, the petition is allowed, and the FIR No. 238/2020, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Ghazipur and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the court of Ms. Shazadi Halima, ,
learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahila Court (East), Karkardooma Courts, Delhi,
is hereby quashed.
